## Evaluation of $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\left(\frac{\sin x}{x}\right)^{2}dx$ via Plancherel's Theorem

**Fourier transform convention.** We use
$$
\widehat{f}(\xi)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,e^{-2\pi i x\xi}\,dx,
\qquad
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}|f(x)|^{2}\,dx=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}|\widehat{f}(\xi)|^{2}\,d\xi
\quad\text{(Plancherel).}
$$

**Step 1. A basic Fourier pair.** Let $\Pi=\mathbf{1}_{[-1/2,\,1/2]}$ be the rectangular function. A direct computation gives
$$
\widehat{\Pi}(\xi)=\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}e^{-2\pi i x\xi}\,dx
=\frac{\sin(\pi\xi)}{\pi\xi}
=:\operatorname{sinc}(\xi).
$$

**Step 2. Identify $f(x)=\frac{\sin x}{x}$ as a Fourier transform.** Observe
$$
\operatorname{sinc}\!\left(\frac{x}{\pi}\right)
=\frac{\sin\!\bigl(\pi\cdot\frac{x}{\pi}\bigr)}{\pi\cdot\frac{x}{\pi}}
=\frac{\sin x}{x}.
$$
So $f(x)=\frac{\sin x}{x}=\operatorname{sinc}(x/\pi)=\widehat{\Pi}(x/\pi)$.

Using the scaling law $\widehat{f(a\,\cdot\,)}(\xi)=\frac{1}{|a|}\widehat{f}(\xi/a)$ in the reverse direction: if we set
$$
g(\xi)=\pi\,\Pi(\pi\xi)=\pi\,\mathbf{1}_{[-1/(2\pi),\,1/(2\pi)]}(\xi),
$$
then
$$
\widehat{g}(x)=\pi\cdot\frac{1}{\pi}\,\widehat{\Pi}\!\left(\frac{x}{\pi}\right)=\widehat{\Pi}\!\left(\frac{x}{\pi}\right)=\frac{\sin x}{x}=f(x).
$$
Thus $f=\widehat{g}$.

**Step 3. Apply Plancherel.** Since $f=\widehat{g}$, Plancherel (and the unitarity of the Fourier transform, so $\int|\widehat{g}|^{2}=\int|g|^{2}$) yields
$$
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\left(\frac{\sin x}{x}\right)^{2}dx
=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}|f(x)|^{2}\,dx
=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}|g(\xi)|^{2}\,d\xi.
$$
Now $g(\xi)=\pi$ on $\left[-\frac{1}{2\pi},\frac{1}{2\pi}\right]$ and $0$ elsewhere, so
$$
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}|g(\xi)|^{2}\,d\xi
=\int_{-1/(2\pi)}^{1/(2\pi)}\pi^{2}\,d\xi
=\pi^{2}\cdot\frac{1}{\pi}
=\pi.
$$

**Conclusion.**
$$
\boxed{\displaystyle\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\left(\frac{\sin x}{x}\right)^{2}dx=\pi.}
$$
